heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF TOLITOLI REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb.
2. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
3. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
4. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully;
5. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
6. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
7. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
8. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will or has occurred;
9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
10. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
11. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is or has occurred.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, guidance techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping someone recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a way out or efforts to overcome these problems.
16. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
17. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, society, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
19. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
20. Social Welfare Implementation Institution hereinafter abbreviated as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out the implementation of social welfare for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
21. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
22. Region is Tolitoli Regency.
23. Regent is the Regent of Tolitoli.
24. Regional Government is the Regent of Tolitoli as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
25. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent of Tolitoli and the Regional House of Representatives in the Implementation of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Regency Region.
26. Regional House of Representatives of Tolitoli Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.

heading: Article 7

Article 8

1. The Regional Government is obliged to prepare Prevention programs or activities as referred to in Article 7 in the Regional Work Plan and Regional Strategic Plan.
2. Programs or activities as referred to in paragraph (1) are to support the realization of the Regional Long-Term Development Plan and Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.

Integrated Services for Victims of Acts of Violence

heading: Article 9
Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. Complaint services as referred to in Article 9 paragraph (1) letter a shall be implemented to receive reports of acts of Violence.
2. Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) may come from:
a. victims;
b. referrals; or
c. outreach.

heading: Article 11
Article 12
Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

1. Repatriation and social reintegration as referred to in Article 9 paragraph (1) letter i shall be implemented with the following principles:
a. voluntary;
b. safe and dignified;
c. respect for rights.
2. In the event that the regional government is not yet able to implement repatriation and social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1), it may request assistance from related parties.
3. Social services to provide social welfare for Children in conflict with the law shall be carried out by the Regional Government together with LPKS and other social institutions.
4. LPKS and other social institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) are rehabilitation and temporary shelter facilities for Children in conflict with the law before repatriation and social reintegration are implemented.

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. Empowerment of Victims of Violence as referred to in Article 2 paragraph (2) letter c carried out by the Regional Government in the form of:
a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and
c. capital assistance.
2. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

Stages of protection for Child Victims of Violence, include:
a. prevention of acts of Violence against Children;
b. handling of Child Victims of Violence; and
c. rehabilitation of Child Victims of Violence.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Prevention of Violence Against Children

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. Prevention of acts of Violence against Children as referred to in Article 15 letter a shall be implemented by:
a. forming a network in efforts to prevent Violence against Children;
b. coordinating, integrating, synchronizing the prevention of Violence based on partnership patterns with the community, private sector and Non-Governmental Organizations; and
c. disseminating laws and regulations related to the protection of Child Victims of Violence.
2. Prevention of acts of Violence against Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus having the principal duties and functions in the field of Women's empowerment and Child protection.

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to Women and Children from acts of Violence are the joint responsibility of the Regional Government and the Community.

heading: Article 26
CHAPTER VII
Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. The Regional Government encourages the business world to participate in the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of:
a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of Violence against Women and Children; and
b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

INFORMATION AND REPORTING SYSTEM

Article 29

1. The Regional Government prepares and compiles an information and reporting system for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. The information and reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 30

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of P2TP2A.
2. Guidance and supervision is carried out by the Regional Apparatus with duties and responsibilities in the field of Women's empowerment and Child protection.
3. The results of the implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) must be reported to the Regional Government.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

FUNDING

Article 31

Funding for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence, may be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
b. other lawful sources that are non-binding in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. The Regional Government may provide funding assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
2. Funding assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with regional financial capacity and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 33

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Tolitoli Regency.

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF TOLITOLI REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

The Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia states that the State has an obligation to provide protection to every citizen. Article 28 G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia explicitly states that: every person has the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, and has the right to a sense of security and protection from threats of fear to do or not do something which is a human right. Violence is a manifestation of human emotional behavior, rather than rational behavior.

In the context of protection for victims of crime, there are preventive and repressive efforts carried out, both by the community and the government (through its law enforcement apparatus), such as providing protection or supervision from various threats that may endanger the victim's life, providing medical assistance, as well as adequate legal assistance. Protection means sheltering something from dangerous things, that something can be an interest or an object or goods. In addition, protection also contains the meaning of shelter provided by someone to someone who is weaker. Thus, legal protection can be interpreted as all government efforts to ensure legal certainty to provide protection to its citizens so that their rights as citizens are not violated, and those who violate them can be subject to sanctions in accordance with applicable regulations.

heading: Article 5

translated_text:
Article 5

Letter a What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.

Letter b What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter c What is meant by "economic violence" is an act that restricts humans from working inside or outside the home to produce money and goods, including allowing humans who work to be exploited, while someone does not fulfill the economic needs of the family.

Letter d What is meant by "social violence" is an act of a person or group of people that causes injury or loss of life to a person or can cause physical damage or damage to another person's property.

Letter e What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter f What is meant by "Domestic Neglect" is:
a. actions that result in non-fulfillment;
b. the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social;
c. actions that deliberately neglect to maintain, care for, or take care of children as they should;
d. actions that neglect people within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person;
e. actions that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter g Sufficiently clear.

Letter h What is meant by "threat of certain actions" is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.

Letter b What is meant by "health services" is efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.

Letter c Sufficiently clear.

Letter e What is meant by "spiritual guidance" is a form of activity in which there is a process of spiritual guidance and development for humans so that it can provide peace, tranquility and coolness of heart to humans by always providing encouragement and motivation to remain patient, trust in God and continue to carry out their obligations.

Letter f What is meant by "social rehabilitation services" is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

Letter g What is meant by "legal aid and assistance services" is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that are gender sensitive.

Letter h Sufficiently clear.

Letter i What is meant by "repatriation and reintegration" is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
